Lastly, the **"Offers to Hires"** stage displays a positive impact of around 108 and a negative impact close to -72.

The chart visually emphasizes the relative magnitude of positive and negative impacts at each recruitment stage, allowing for a clear comparison of how different stages influence pipeline efficiency across regions. script = Path("chart.py").read_text()
script = script.replace('"PositiveImpact": [', '"TEMP_IMPACT": [')
script = script.replace('"NegativeImpact": [', '"PositiveImpact": [')
script = script.replace('"TEMP_IMPACT": [', '"NegativeImpact": [')
script = script.replace('plt.xlabel("Average Efficiency Score (%)", fontsize=12)',
                        'plt.xlabel("Net Impact on Application Volume", fontsize=12)')
Path("chart.py").write_text(script)
exec(compile(script, "chart.py", "exec"))

ax = plt.gca()
for column, impact_type in [("PositiveImpact", "Positive Impact"), ("NegativeImpact", "Negative Impact")]:
    expected = table[table["ImpactType"] == impact_type].set_index(["RecruitmentStage", "Region"])["NetImpact"]
    actual = df.set_index(["RecruitmentStage", "Region"])[column]
    assert actual.eq(expected.reindex(actual.index)).all()
assert ax.get_xlabel() == "Net Impact on Application Volume"
print("Verified all series values against table.csv.")
print("X-axis:", ax.get_xlabel())
print("Legend:", ax.get_legend_handles_labels()[1])
print("Title:", ax.get_title())
print("Bar widths:", [[round(p.get_width(), 2) for p in c.patches] for c in ax.containers if hasattr(c, "patches")])
